The studio was called "Eternal Serenity," a name that felt increasingly ironic as Jim, a man whose idea of stretching was reaching for the remote, sat in the back row. He had intended to join the "Gentle Morning Flow," but due to a misread sign and a profound lack of spatial awareness, he had walked into the "Advanced Inversions & Acrobatics" session.

The instructor, a woman named Seraphina who looked like she was carved from marble and patience, clapped her hands. "Welcome, seekers of truth. Today, we explore the Giraffe Pose. It requires balance, grace, and an elongation of the spirit."

Jim looked around. Everyone else was already standing on one leg, arms extended like elegant branches. He looked at his own limbs, which resembled overcooked spaghetti. He decided to mimic the woman next to him, who was currently balancing on her forehead while humming a low B-flat.

Jim attempted to lift his leg. He missed his balance entirely. As he flailed, his body contorted into a shape that defied both anatomy and dignity. He let out a grunt that sounded like a deflating tire.

"Focus on your breath, Jim," Seraphina said, gliding over. She didn't look angry; she looked disappointed, which was worse.

"I am focusing," Jim wheezed, his face turning a shade of purple usually reserved for bruised plums. He tried to correct his posture by leaning forward, but his center of gravity was located somewhere near his knees. As he leaned, a pressure built in his lower abdomen—a side effect of the kale smoothie he’d had for breakfast and the sheer terror of being in the wrong class.

He tried to suppress it. He really did. But the yoga pose he was attempting, which he thought was called "The Tree," was actually "The Falling Log," and the physical compression was undeniable.

*Pfft.*

It wasn't a loud noise. It was a subtle, high-pitched squeak, like a rubber duck being stepped on by a giant.

The entire class froze. The woman on her forehead stopped humming. The man doing a handstand paused mid-pose, his legs wobbling dangerously.

Seraphina closed her eyes. "The body speaks," she said calmly. "Listen to its truth."
